d: A storage adapter that keeps the configuration items in the Google Drive of the user, with a local copy in the browser: the application starts at once from the local copy, works without Google, and Drive becomes the reference as soon as the user is connected.
The files of an application in folders of the Google Drive of the user: list a folder, send a file (an image, a PDF, any file dropped by the user), read it back, copy it.

A table kept in a tab of a Google spreadsheet, in the Drive of the user, with a local copy in the browser: the rows are objects whose keys are the headers of the tab; one column (key) identifies them.
Storage adapter for config: a local copy, and the Google Drive of the user.
The files of an application in folders of Google Drive.
A table in a tab of a Google spreadsheet, with a local copy.

The connection to a Google account, and the calls to the APIs of Google (Drive, Sheets, Tasks…) with its token: an application without any server reaches the data of its user in the user's own Google account.
The connection to a Google account.
An error answered by an API of Google.

A storage adapter that keeps the configuration items in the local database of the browser (IndexedDB): they survive a reload of the page and a restart of the browser, on this computer and in this browser only, without any server.
Storage adapter for config, in the local database of the browser.
A storage adapter that keeps the configuration items in memory: nothing survives a reload of the page.
Storage adapter for config, in memory.
Actions declared in HTML: a click on an element runs the actions written in its data-* attributes, without any JavaScript in the component.
The synchronous event bus: every event of Ricochet goes through it, whether it is emitted now, deferred as a microtask or scheduled for later (see docs/DESIGN.md, principles 1 to 3).
The two clocks of the kernel, in milliseconds.
The store of configuration items: shared, persistent key/value pairs.
A store of configuration items.
Styles written next to the component that uses them.
Debugging tools of the kernel, installed when the module is imported, and the functions an application uses to add its own.
The display mode of the application: pc or phone.
A synchronous event bus.
The frame loop.
Game time.
The debugging state of the kernel, shared with the console as window.$global: debug switches, recent logs, error counters and leak counters.
The store of configuration items used by the kernel (observeItems(), setItem(), the keyboard…).
Centralised, layered keyboard handling.
The keyboard controller.
The frame loop: one requestAnimationFrame loop for the whole page, that runs only when something needs it.
Microtasks: events deferred to the spare time of the frames.
A queue of microtasks.

The changes not saved yet in a remote store (Google Drive, Google Tasks, a server…): each adapter that keeps changes before it sends them reports how many it holds and what it is doing; the kernel adds them up and announces the total by one event.
The register of the changes not saved yet.

The log of the requests: every request that the application sends (to its server, to a web service, to Google Drive…) is recorded in the log ajax of debugging ($global.logs.ajax, the last 100 entries, the newest first) and in the timeline, with its time.
The router: hash routing (#universe/brick/…), which works on any static host, GitHub Pages included.
The router.
Scheduled tasks: events due at a given time, in real time or in game time (see the clock module).
The scheduled tasks.
The store of secrets: API keys, tokens, passwords that the user gives to the application, and that must stay on this computer.
A store of secrets.
The store of the session: state that lives as long as the tab, survives a reload of the page, and is not worth a configuration item (the pages seen lately, the place in a list, a draft).
A store of session values.
The entry point of an application (principle 9 of docs/DESIGN.md):
The time spent on an activity, in milliseconds: real time, counted only while the page is visible.
WComponent: a controller bound to a DOM element.
WController: the base class of everything that reacts to events without owning a DOM element (keyboard, data proxies, business logic).
Base class of components bound to a DOM element.
Base class of controllers.
Every component of the interface, the theme and the icon set, from one import.
The entry point of the kernel: the classes and functions an application uses, from one import, without knowing the folders of Ricochet.
The entry point of the utilities: dates, texts, numbers, random numbers, noise, complex numbers, identifiers, debounce and throttle, and a few tools for games.
Icon set drawn by hand on a common 24 × 24 grid.
A resolver for the router (see the router module) that organises an application in universes and bricks: #universe/brick/….
The look shared by the components that hold a <button>: rc-icon-button, rc-text-button, and rc-checkbox and rc-radio, which look like flat buttons.

The look shared by the fields: rc-input, rc-textarea, rc-combobox and rc-select, and the fields of an application that extend rc-input under their own tag (their element has the class rc-field, added by rc-input).
A breadcrumb: rc-breadcrumb holds rc-crumb elements, each a step of the path, shown on one line with a separator between them.
A checkbox: an rc-icon-button whose icon shows a state, checked or not.
A field of free text with suggestions: the user chooses a value of the list, or types a new one.
A modal window: a native <dialog>, shown above the page, which is greyed and cannot be used until the window closes.
A button that opens a window below it: a menu, a filter, a small form.
Floating buttons: round buttons that stay at the bottom of the screen while the view scrolls, for the actions of the view (next card, edit, save…).
An icon of the icon set (icons/iconset.mjs), drawn in the colour of the text: it follows the palette of its block, by day and by night.
A button made of an icon and an optional label.
An image that has no address the browser can load: a file of Google Drive read with a token, an image kept in IndexedDB, a file dropped by the user and not yet sent.
A one-line input field.
The grid of a month: the names of the days, then the weeks, Monday first, each day a button.
Radio buttons: a group, rc-radio-group, holds the value; each rc-radio inside it offers one value.
A choice in a list: a native <select>, so that every browser shows its own list (a wheel on a phone).
A slider: a number between two bounds, chosen by moving a thumb along a track.
Tabs: rc-tabs holds rc-tab elements, each with the content of one tab.
A button made of text, or of any content: a click runs the actions of its data-* attributes (see the actions module).
A field of several lines, whose height follows its content.
The component of <rc-breadcrumb>.
The component of <rc-checkbox>.
The component of <rc-combobox>: the attributes of rc-input, and the ones below.
The component of <rc-crumb>: a step of a breadcrumb.
The component of <rc-dialog>.
The component of <rc-dropdown>.
The component of <rc-floating-bar>: the line of the floating buttons, at the end of the view.
The component of <rc-floating-button>: a round icon button.
The component of <rc-floating-group>: floating buttons side by side, with their keys and their colours.
The component of <rc-icon>.
The component of <rc-icon-button>.
The component of <rc-image>.
The component of <rc-input>.
The component of <rc-month>.
The component of <rc-radio>: one radio button of an rc-radio-group.
The component of <rc-radio-group>: holds the value of its radios.
The component of <rc-select>.
The component of <rc-slider>.
The component of <rc-tab>: the content of one tab.
The component of <rc-tabs>.
The component of <rc-textarea>.
The component of <rc-text-button>.
The look of the tables of an application: a class on <table>, rc-table, and classes that adjust it.
Colours of the interface: palettes, shades, day and night.
The theme: applies the configuration item ricochet-theme to the page.

A canvas with a fixed logical size (a game of 1200 × 600, say), scaled by CSS to the width of its container, and sharp on a high density screen; and the conversion of a pointer event into logical coordinates.
Functions on objects, arrays and sets, for the cases the language does not cover.
Complex numbers: z = r + i·i, or in polar form z = mod · e^(i·arg).
A complex number.
Calendar dates, without hours and without time zones: a birthday, a due date, the day of a note.
Small helpers around the DOM and the browser: escaping text for HTML, building elements from HTML strings, sanitizing HTML of external origin, and the clipboard.

Overlap tests of simple shapes, for the collisions of a game: circles, axis-aligned rectangles and points, given as plain objects — the entities of the game are tested as they are; and the bounce of a moving circle (a ball) on a rectangle (a brick, a paddle, a wall).
WebGPU: the device shared by the page, the reason when there is none, and two shortcuts for buffers and canvases.
Hashes of texts and data.

Short unique identifiers, made of lowercase letters: 'aa', 'ab'… 'az', 'ba'… They are cheap to make (no random draw, no clock) and short to store, which suits the records of an application or the entities of a game.
A generator of unique identifiers.
Converts Ricochet Markdown to HTML.
Small functions on numbers: bounds, interpolation, angles, rounding.
Noise: numbers that vary smoothly with their coordinates, for landscapes, clouds, textures or wandering moves.
A pool of objects: many short-lived objects (particles, bullets, sparks) are taken from the pool and given back to it, instead of being created and left to the garbage collector.
A pool of reusable objects.
Gradient noise (Ken Perlin's improved noise), in one, two or three dimensions, with octaves.
A quadtree of points: a rectangle split into four when it holds too many points, and so on.
A quadtree of points (an index and its coordinates).
Pseudo-random numbers that can be replayed: the same seed gives the same sequence, on every browser.
A generator of pseudo-random numbers.

A full-text search made simple: the terms of a text (searchTerms), kept with the record that holds them, and an index that finds the records holding all the terms of a query, each one as the beginning of a word (SearchIndex).
An index of records by their search terms; a query finds the records holding all its terms.

The sounds of a game, with the Web Audio API: each file is loaded and decoded once for the page, then played as often as needed, several at the same time, without any pool of <audio> elements to size.
Sounds that can be played by name.
The neighbours of a point among thousands, without comparing every pair: the points are sorted into the cells of a grid, and a search only visits the cells around the point.
A grid of cells for the search of neighbours.
An animation cut from a sheet of frames.
The images of a game: loading them before the game starts, drawing one centred on a point (turned, scaled), and the animations cut from a sheet of frames.
Functions on texts.

The d attribute of an SVG <path>, as a list of segments: read it (with the place of the first error), write it back (plain or compact), turn its commands absolute or relative, round its numbers, move, scale, turn or mirror it, and check it against the drawing rules of the icon set (iconset).
Debounce and throttle: calls that come in bursts (keys typed, a window resized, a slider dragged) turned into few events.
Value noise, as the noise() function of p5.js: a table of 4 096 random values, interpolated, in several octaves.
Ricochet keeps a few settings in the configuration items of the application (see the config module).
This guide lists what Ricochet offers to see what an application does: switches that show messages in the console, logs of the last events, error counters, a leak detector.
The principles Ricochet is built on, and the decisions taken while extracting it from SweetHome.
Ricochet emits and listens to a few events on the bus.

Ricochet uses a restricted Markdown: a subset of GitHub Flavored Markdown that any Markdown reader (GitHub, VSCode, Obsidian…) displays correctly, and that Ricochet converts to HTML in a single pass with regular expressions (src/utils/markdown.mjs).
This guide explains how the colours of an interface built with Ricochet are chosen, and how an application gives its interface a look of its own: palettes, shades, day and night, shadows.

This guide explains how to set up an application on top of Ricochet: getting the files, loading them, starting the application, running it on your computer, a phone version, and documenting your own code.
